title: Daniel Pink's Scientific Secrets of Perfect Timing
one_liner: A comedic summary of Daniel Pink's 'When' reveals how to schedule your day around your natural energy cycles.
key_points: Most people peak analytically in the morning — schedule focused, analytical work then and creative work in the afternoon
Everyone follows a peak → trough → recovery cycle; the 1–4 p.m. slump is ideal for low-stakes tasks like emails
Optimal productivity ratio is ~52 minutes of work followed by 17 minutes of break
Timing matters beyond work: morning surgeries have fewer errors, morning court appearances get more lenient rulings, and workout timing depends on whether you're a morning or evening person
